title: Is this Chinese Bike Good Or Just Good For The Money?

takeaways.text: Clearance is 32 mm, which the tester calls enough for now but not future-proof; he would have liked 35 mm.
The size-L (about 56) 105 Di2 build weighed just over 8.3 kg with pedals and bottle cages; it cost about £3,500–4,000.
Stack is about 15 mm lower than a Tarmac SL9 or Giant Propel, with a relatively slack 72.3° head angle and 4–8 mm more trail, so it is very stable at speed but less reactive when climbing.
He had significant toe overlap even on the stock 28 mm tires with rearward cleats, so wider tires make it worse.
Bikes are built to order with chosen wheels, bar width, stem, chainrings, cassette and crank length; UK buyers must collect from Winspace's Bridgend workshop.
Compromises: Shimano RT64-class rotors that squeal when hot, a SUMC chain whose wear life he doubts, Continental clincher tires on inner tubes, and integrated-bar tops with sharp edges underneath.
He would be tempted by the frameset at about £1,300 (roughly US$1,600).

disclosure: Publication review of a Winspace test bike; how the bike was supplied is not stated in the video.
summary: BikeRadar's ride review of a size-L Winspace M6 with Shimano 105 Di2, covering clearance, weight, geometry, customization and component compromises.
